title: JEE Main 2026 (April 2nd, Shift 2) - Chemistry - The d- and f-Block Elements
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Among $Fe^{2+}$, $Fe^{3+}$, $Cr^{2+}$ and $Zn^{2+}$, the ion that shows positive borax bead test and with highest ionisation enthalpy is:
questions.explain: Zn compounds are typically white or colourless and do not show a coloured borax bead test. Iron and chromium form coloured beads (positive test). Among $Fe^{2+}$, $Cr^{2+}$, and $Fe^{3+}$, the $Fe^{3+}$ ion has a half-filled, exceptionally stable $3d^5$ configuration. Its further ionization to $Fe^{4+}$ requires a significantly larger amount of energy (highest consecutive ionization enthalpy among the listed accessible oxidation states). Therefore, $Fe^{3+}$ is the correct answer.

questions.q:
Number of paramagnetic ions among the following d- and f-block metal ions is _______.
$Mn^{2+}, Cu^{2+}, Zn^{2+}, Yb^{2+}, Sc^{3+}, La^{3+}, Gd^{3+}, Lu^{3+}, Ti^{4+}, Ce^{4+}$
(Atomic numbers of Mn = 25, Cu = 29, Zn = 30, Yb = 70, Sc = 21, La = 57, Gd = 64, Lu = 71, Ti = 22, Ce = 58)
questions.explain:
Paramagnetic ions must possess unpaired electrons:
- $Mn^{2+} (3d^5)$ : 5 unpaired electrons (Paramagnetic)
- $Cu^{2+} (3d^9)$ : 1 unpaired electron (Paramagnetic)
- $Zn^{2+} (3d^{10})$ : 0 unpaired electrons (Diamagnetic)
- $Yb^{2+} (4f^{14})$ : 0 unpaired electrons (Diamagnetic)
- $Sc^{3+} (3d^0)$ : 0 unpaired electrons (Diamagnetic)
- $La^{3+} (4f^0)$ : 0 unpaired electrons (Diamagnetic)
- $Gd^{3+} (4f^7)$ : 7 unpaired electrons (Paramagnetic)
- $Lu^{3+} (4f^{14})$ : 0 unpaired electrons (Diamagnetic)
- $Ti^{4+} (3d^0)$ : 0 unpaired electrons (Diamagnetic)
- $Ce^{4+} (4f^0)$ : 0 unpaired electrons (Diamagnetic)
Total number of paramagnetic ions is 3.
